content.stem: If 4, 10 and \(x\) are in continued proportion, then the value of \(x\) is:

steps.title: Write the proportion
steps.explanation: In a continued proportion \(a : b = b : c\), so \(x\) is the third proportional to 4 and 10.
steps.rule: If \(a, b, c\) are in continued proportion, \(b^2 = ac\).

commonMistakes: Writing the proportion the wrong way round, \(x = \tfrac{4^2}{10} = 1.6\), option (a).
Finding the mean proportional \(\sqrt{4 \times 10} = 2\sqrt{10}\) instead of the third proportional, option (b).
Treating the numbers as an arithmetic progression (adding 6 each time) to get 16, option (c).

questions.authorNotes: Distractors correspond to the three errors listed in commonMistakes.

content.stem:
Using the property of componendo and dividendo, solve for \(x\):
\[ \frac{\sqrt{x + 1} + \sqrt{x - 4}}{\sqrt{x + 1} - \sqrt{x - 4}} = 5 \]

hints: If \(\frac{a}{b} = \frac{c}{d}\), then \(\frac{a + b}{a - b} = \frac{c + d}{c - d}\). Write 5 as \(\frac{5}{1}\).
After applying the property, the expression simplifies to \(\frac{\sqrt{x+1}}{\sqrt{x-4}}\). Square both sides.

solution.modelAnswer: By componendo and dividendo, \(\dfrac{2\sqrt{x+1}}{2\sqrt{x-4}} = \dfrac{5 + 1}{5 - 1} = \dfrac{3}{2}\). Squaring, \(\dfrac{x + 1}{x - 4} = \dfrac{9}{4}\), so \(4x + 4 = 9x - 36\), \(5x = 40\), \(x = 8\). Check: \(\dfrac{3 + 2}{3 - 2} = 5\).

steps.title: Apply componendo and dividendo
steps.explanation: Write the right-hand side as \(\frac{5}{1}\) and apply the property to both sides.
steps.rule: If \(\frac{a}{b} = \frac{c}{d}\), then \(\frac{a + b}{a - b} = \frac{c + d}{c - d}\).

steps.title: Simplify
steps.explanation: The \(\sqrt{x-4}\) terms cancel in the numerator and the \(\sqrt{x+1}\) terms cancel in the denominator.

steps.title: Square both sides
steps.explanation: Squaring removes the square roots; then cross-multiply.

steps.title: Solve and check
steps.explanation: Check: \(\sqrt{9} = 3\) and \(\sqrt{4} = 2\), so the left-hand side is \(\frac{3 + 2}{3 - 2} = 5\). The value satisfies the equation.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to write 5 as \(\tfrac{5}{1}\) and computing \(\tfrac{5+5}{5-5}\) or similar.
Not squaring both sides fully, e.g. writing \(\tfrac{x+1}{x-4} = \tfrac{3}{2}\).
Sign errors when cross-multiplying: \(4(x + 1) = 9(x - 4)\) gives \(4x + 4 = 9x - 36\), not \(9x + 36\).

criteria.description: Correct use of componendo and dividendo
commonErrors: Applying the property to one side only

criteria.description: Squares and forms a linear equation
acceptedAlternatives: Second application of componendo and dividendo: (2x − 3)/5 = 13/5
criteria.partialCreditRules: Award if the squaring is correct following an arithmetic slip in the ratio.

questions.authorNotes: The question instructs students to use componendo and dividendo; a student who solves by cross-multiplying and rationalising may need the reviewer to decide whether to award the method mark. x = 8 lies in the domain (x ≥ 4) and was checked by substitution.
